physicalEvidence.status: Verified prior-Northeastern learned navigation, physical20; current Michigan robot access unknown
physicalEvidence.summary: Full SPARTA 2025 methods verify a PointPillars/convolutional risk model whose Fourier coefficients describe approach-angle-conditioned terrain risk; CVaR feeds MPPI on an actual AgileX Scout Mini. A prebuilt point-cloud map and onboard RTX4070 are used. In five physical trials the method selected the safe route; the dangerous alternative obstacle was virtual, deliberately avoiding vehicle damage. Training tire-deformation labels and the large boulder-field benchmark are simulation. This is prior-Northeastern collaborative hardware, not verified current Michigan apparatus.

name: Zach J. Patterson
title: Assistant Professor (January 2025–)
department: Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering; Cybernetics and Physical Intelligence Lab
fitReason: Recently hired Assistant Professor with directly attributable learned physical robot work, including motion imitation and neural visual tracking. Current CWRU PhD supervision is independently visible; verified apparatus belongs to collaborative MIT-based projects.

physicalEvidence.status: Verified collaborative MIT-site learned swimming/visual-servo execution, physical20; CWRU apparatus not independently verified
physicalEvidence.summary: The full July 2025 OSMP study learns diffeomorphic motion encoders from demonstrations and deploys them on arms, a soft manipulator and a swimming turtle; author contributions explicitly credit Patterson with turtle experiments and project supervision. The February 2026 turtle paper separately connects SAM/CUTIE tracking to visual-servo gait commands in pool trials, with human target initialization/correction. Its untethered obstacle avoidance uses classical stereo and must not be described as onboard neural autonomy. MIT pool/New England Aquarium sites are acknowledged; no current CWRU learned-hardware setup is established.
